ts9_israel.topic: Israel's side of the Christian Zionist alliance: courtship by governments, tourism, IFCJ money, the 2025 campaign

claims.text: In November 1980 Prime Minister Menachem Begin presented the Jabotinsky Centennial Medal, awarded by the Jabotinsky Foundation of New York to 100 Americans, at a dinner in New York; Jerry Falwell was a recipient; Senator Frank Church declined his award in protest at Falwell's receiving it.

Rabbi Marc Tanenbaum (Detroit Jewish News, 18 Sep 1981) wrote that Begin 'agreed to meet with the Rev. Jerry Falwell' on his US visit and criticised the 'singling out of Rev. Falwell as the only American Christian leader', pointing to some 30 million evangelicals outside the Moral Majority's politics.

Christian Century (4 Nov 1998): in January 1998 Netanyahu's first meeting in Washington was with Falwell and more than 1,000 fundamentalist Christians, who called him 'the Ronald Reagan of Israel'; Falwell pledged to contact more than 200,000 evangelical pastors to 'tell President Clinton to refrain from putting pressure on Israel'.

JTA/J. (10 Jun 2021): Netanyahu addressed a Voices United for Israel conference (caption: 19 Jan 1998) convened partly by Falwell: 'We have no greater friends and allies than the people sitting in this room'; the association with Falwell reportedly damaged his relationship with Clinton.

JTA (archive date Feb 1999): Falwell said 'We pledged to help him from our pulpits and our media ministries'; ADL's Leon Klenicki said evangelicals get 'a much warmer welcome' from Likud than Labor governments; Yechiel Eckstein said most evangelicals are 'apolitical'; the Southern Baptist Convention distanced itself.

Ron Dermer (2021): 'the backbone of Israel's support in the United States is the evangelical Christians'; CUFI spokesman Ari Morgenstern: 'Christian Zionists have had a relationship with every prime minister since Ben-Gurion'; John Hagee Ministries (separate from CUFI) has directed $100 million to Israeli charities, including right-wing and settlement groups.

Israel's tourism ministry (2013 data): 3.54 million visitor entries; Christians 53% of tourists staying over one night and about 60% of all visitors (over 2 million); of Christian tourists 49% Catholic, 28% Orthodox, 20% Protestant (mostly evangelical); about 40% called themselves pilgrims; the US was the top source of Christian tourism.

Christian Post (c. early 2009): nearly 1.8 million of 3 million visitors the previous year were Christians; US Christian visitors up 40% from 2000 to 2008; Christians one-third of American visitors; ministry ran a 'Visit Israel – You'll Never Be the Same' campaign with Christian personalities Jack Hayford and Kay Arthur and outreach to US church leaders.

Vatican News/KNA (2 Dec 2024): about 4.5 million tourists in 2019 (record); foreign visitors in 2024 down about three-quarters to 900,000; Catholic pilgrim groups fell from about 16,000 (613,300 pilgrims) in 2019 to under 2,000 (about 56,000) in 2024.

IFCJ, founded by Yechiel Eckstein in 1983, raised more than $1.4 billion mostly from evangelical donors, about $140 million a year; 98% of some 800,000 donors a decade earlier were Christian; claims nearly 2 million supporters; credited with helping more than 730,000 Jews move to Israel; Eckstein said many Jews viewed evangelical support as 'utilitarian'.

MinistryWatch (11 Sep 2020): IFCJ revenue peaked above $135M in 2015 and was $117M in 2019; at least $1.5bn since 1983; fundraising over $19M in 2019 (more than 16% of revenue); fundraising and management just under 30% of revenue; Eckstein paid over $700,000 a year; MinistryWatch issued a donor alert from 2013; IFCJ cancelled a Jerusalem outreach centre after raising tens of millions.

Responsible Statecraft (7 Oct 2025): Show Faith by Works, a new firm, had a $3.2M contract with the Israeli government (overseen by MFA chief of staff Eran Shayovich, via Havas Media) to geofence major churches in California, Arizona, Nevada and Colorado and Christian colleges, aiming at about 3.8 million churchgoers; Chad Schnitger said the plan was 'an early planning document' and 'Everything we do is vetted through teams of Christian pastors'.

ts9_us.topic: The US side: the evangelical vote, stated motives, publishing and donors

claims.text: Pew (American Trends Panel, reported 15 Sep 2021): white evangelical voters backed Trump 77% in 2016 and 84% in 2020; white adults identifying as evangelical rose from 25% to 29%.
CNN exit poll (via RNS, 6 Nov 2024): white born-again/evangelical voters 81% for Trump in 2024, 76% in 2020, 80% in 2016.
Ryan Burge (Cooperative Election Study): white evangelicals about 77% Trump in 2016, 81% in 2020, 83% in 2024, the highest on record; Burge notes exit polls have design flaws.
Pew validated-voter study (26 Jun 2025, about 7,100 validated voters): white evangelical support for Trump in 2024 'no different' from 2020; Protestants overall 62%, up 3 points.
Trump at a rally in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, 17 Aug 2020, on the Jerusalem embassy: 'That's for the evangelicals'; 'The evangelicals are more excited about that than Jewish people.'

Sarah Posner (Democracy Now, 15 Nov 2023): 'At the heart of Christian Zionism is not a love for Israel but rather Christian nationalism'; Hagee's movement gives Israel's defenders a constituency with 'the ear of the Republican Party'; she said Hagee treats Israel as 'just a pawn' in prophecy.

David Brog (CUFI executive director), 7 Sep 2017: 'Christians support Israel for the most noble of motives'; support 'starts with the Bible, but it does not end with the Bible'; evangelicals do not believe they control the timing of Jesus's return; a John Hagee Ministries gift to Im Tirtzu predated knowledge of its views.

Ari Morgenstern (CUFI), 2 Aug 2010: most Christian Zionists support Israel because of Genesis's promise that God will bless those who bless the Jewish people; Hagee reads Matthew 24:36 as meaning humans cannot hasten the end, so eschatology cannot be the motive.

+972 (Alex Kane, 13 Jan 2021), from Adelson Family Foundation tax filings: Adelson gave CUFI $4.6 million since 2012 and the Maccabee Task Force (founded 2015, led by former CUFI director David Brog) about $22.1 million.

claims.text: Netanyahu addressed the 8 July 2019 CUFI summit remotely from Jerusalem.

Democracy Now: the line 'At the heart of Christian Zionism is not a love for Israel but rather Christian nationalism' is from Posner's writing, read by Juan Gonzalez; Posner said Hagee 'has basically hoodwinked many Jews into believing that he actually supports Israel'.
Brog (7 Sep 2017, Congregation Emanu-El): evangelicals reject replacement theology; CUFI members know Jews better than other Christians and so are more sensitive to Jewish aversion to proselytising.

MinistryWatch: IFCJ paid nearly $8 million in 2018 to The Bigham Agency, a direct-response firm; the International Center for Christian Outreach was cancelled after Eckstein's death and falling revenue.

Tanenbaum 1981 counted 'an estimated 30 million "mainline" Evangelicals', 50 million Roman Catholics and 'some 45 million liberal Protestants'; the news item on the same page says Begin 'agreed to meet with the Rev. Jerry Falwell'.
